t: Carved out of Alexander's conquests by his general Seleucus I, the Seleucid Empire stretched from Syria towards India at its height.
Its many new Greek cities spread Hellenistic language and culture across the Near East and Central Asia for centuries.
Defeat by Rome, Parthian conquest of the east and endless dynastic civil war reduced it to a Syrian rump that Pompey annexed in 64-63 BCE.
dyk: Seleucus I traded eastern lands to Chandragupta Maurya for 500 war elephants, which helped him win the Battle of Ipsus in 301 BCE.
ev: Seleucus retakes Babylon after the Battle of Gaza, the starting point of the Seleucid era
Seleucus and Lysimachus defeat and kill Antigonus at the Battle of Ipsus
Seleucus defeats Lysimachus at Corupedium but is assassinated within months
Antiochus III begins a seven-year eastern campaign that earns him the title 'the Great'
Rome routs Antiochus III's army at the Battle of Magnesia
Antiochus IV's suppression of Jewish practice sparks the Maccabean revolt
Mithridates I of Parthia conquers Mesopotamia and captures Seleucia-on-Tigris
Pompey deposes Antiochus XIII and makes Syria a Roman province
